title: Spin-1/2 Heisenberg diamond-like decorated honeycomb lattice in a magnetic field from the perspective of localized magnons and exact diagonalization
authors: Katarina Karlova, Malo Rouxel, Jozef Strecka, Andreas Honecker
abstract: The spin-$1/2$ quantum Heisenberg model on the diamond-decorated honeycomb lattice in a magnetic field is investigated using complementary analytical and numerical methods. The ground-state phase diagram comprises Lieb-Mattis ferrimagnetic, dimer-tetramer, monomer-dimer, spin-canted, and saturated paramagnetic phases, giving rise to characteristic magnetization plateaus, continuous and discontinuous field-induced transitions. In the highly frustrated regime, a localized-magnon approach based on an effective classical lattice-gas model provides an accurate description of the low-temperature magnetism and thermodynamics in agreement with numerical results. At intermediate frustration, finite-temperature calculations reveal characteristic specific-heat signatures of the field-induced transitions including the development of Ising critical behavior at the field-induced transition between the monomer-dimer and Lieb-Mattis ferrimagnetic phase.
summary: This paper thoroughly maps the magnetic phase diagram of a spin-1/2 Heisenberg model on a diamond-decorated honeycomb lattice under a magnetic field. By combining advanced numerical methods like QMC and localized-magnon theory, the authors identify multiple magnetic phases and pinpoint critical behaviors, such as Ising criticality, at field-induced quantum phase transitions.
main_problem: The study investigates the ground-state phase diagram and finite-temperature magnetic properties of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg model on a complex diamond-decorated honeycomb lattice under an external magnetic field.
main_result: The system exhibits five distinct magnetic phases (LM, DT, MD, SC, SP) characterized by magnetization plateaus and field-induced transitions, with specific heat signatures revealing Ising critical behavior at certain crossovers.
method: The research employs a combination of analytical techniques, including a localized-magnon approach mapping to an effective classical lattice-gas model, alongside advanced numerical methods like DMRG, Lanczos Exact Diagonalization (EDL), and Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC).
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1/2 Heisenberg model defined on a diamond-decorated honeycomb lattice. The Hamiltonian includes antiferromagnetic couplings ($J_1, J_2$) and a Zeeman term ($h$), allowing for the mapping to an effective lattice-gas model in the highly frustrated regime.
key_observables: Magnetization plateaus, specific heat ($c$), susceptibility, and entropy.
important_parameters: Interaction ratio ($J_2/J_1$) and magnetic field ratio ($h/J_1$), as well as temperature ($T/J_1$).
main_assumptions: The localized-magnon approach is used for the highly frustrated regime, and comparisons are made between finite-size exact diagonalization/mean-field results and the thermodynamic limit lattice-gas model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic lattice, the full ground-state phase diagram, and specific heat ($c$) vs. magnetic field ($h/J_1$) at various temperatures and coupling ratios, highlighting transition features.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the phase diagram using multiple computational techniques, comparing results across different frustration regimes and temperatures to pinpoint critical behaviors and phase boundaries.
why_interesting: The detailed study of phase transitions, critical exponents (Ising behavior), and the successful mapping to an effective classical model provides deep insights into frustrated quantum magnetism, which is relevant for understanding complex quantum materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic illustration of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg model on a diamond-decorated honeycomb lattice with the green rhombus indicating the unit cell. (b) Ground-state phase diagram in the J2/J1–h/J1 parameter plane, where small yellow (green) ellipses denote singlet (triplet) dimers and large yellow ellipses denote singlet tetramers.

FIG. 2. Representative isothermal magnetization curves calculated for six selected values of the interaction ratio J2/J1 = 0.0, 1.4, 1.6, 2.1, 2.6, and 4.0. Zero-temperature results obtained by DMRG (L = 4) and EDL (L = 2) are compared with finite- temperature QMC (L = 6) and FTLM (L = 2) results at T/J1 = 0.1. For J2/J1 = 4.0, the FTLM results are additionally compared at several temperatures with analytical results derived from the effective lattice-gas model.

FIG. 3. (a) Magnetic susceptibility χ per spin, (b) entropy per unit cell s, and (c) specific heat c per spin as a function of the magnetic field h/J1 for J2/J1 = 4.0 at three selected temperatures. Symbols show the FTLM results for L = 2, while solid lines denote the effective lattice-gas (LG) results in the thermodynamic limit. The legend in (a) applies to all panels.

Figure 3 compares the FTLM results for 32 spins with the thermodynamic-limit lattice-gas description at J2/J1 = 4. The most intriguing features occur at the transition fields h/J1 = 0 and 5. The susceptibility exhibits a single peak at each transition progressively suppressed with increasing temperature, while the entropy behaves similarly with the maxima broadening and gradually increasing with temperature. The specific heat displays a characteristic two-peak structure around h/J1 = 5, whereas only a single peak is observed slightly above zero field.
